parsed.modern: In the time of the Romans, the inhabitants of Cappadocia bore so bad a character, and were reputed so vicious and lewd, that, among the neighbouring nations, a wicked man was emphatically called a Cappadocian. In after ages, however, their lewd disposition was so corrected and restrained by the pure doctrines of Christianity, that no country whatever has produced greater champions of the Christian religion, or given to the church prelates of more unblemished characters.
